s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital swelling with vision deterioration and proptosis
salient_findings: Left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
Progressive deterioration of vision in the left eye
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Left fronto-orbital swelling for 10 years
Progressive vision deterioration in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis became more pronounced over the past month
Left globe displaced inferiorly and medially
No history of endocrine abnormalities
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT
Involvement of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing

shortlist.label: Orbital meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and involvement of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit

shortlist.label: Sphenoid wing meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the sphenoid wing and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof

shortlist.label: Orbital osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the sphenoid wing and destructive bony lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit, including the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing, is most consistent with a sphenoid wing meningioma, which is known to cause such bony changes and orbital displacement.

rejected.label: Orbital meningioma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific involvement of the sphenoid wing and the pattern of bony lesions is more characteristic of a sphenoid wing meningioma.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia can cause bony lesions, but the presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass is not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Orbital osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically well-defined, benign bony growths and do not usually cause the extensive bony destruction or the soft tissue mass seen in this case.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas can occur in the sphenoid region but are less likely to present with the specific pattern of orbital involvement and bony changes described here.

rejected.label: Orbital meningioma
rejected.why: Already considered less likely due to the specific pattern of involvement of the sphenoid wing and surrounding structures.
